It will also be stamped and sealed with the County Clerk seal. There are certain procedures that we must follow to get the document that you ask us to record on the record. We write your name and address and Reception number on the back of the document. Then, the document is scanned into our system so that it shows a clear image of the recording. Any US citizen who is 18 years old or older, who is a New Mexico resident, who has registered to vote, and who is not currently incarcerated may cast a ballot during voting. If you are currently incarcerated in New Mexico for a felony offense you cannot vote while you are incarcerated. However, once you are no longer confined to a jail, prison, or other correctional facility you can register and vote in New Mexico elections. You can register to vote and vote even if you are on probation or parole. You are not required to register to vote in person and, instead, may register by mail, online, at MVD, at state agency offices providing public benefits, through a voter registration agent, or in person. A misdemeanor conviction does not disqualify an individual from registering to vote. Voters with a misdemeanor conviction are not required to register in person and may register to vote through any of the legal registration methods named above. Individuals in jail who are pre-trial (i.e., facing felony charges but not yet convicted) or who have been convicted of a misdemeanor and are serving their sentence in a county jail are eligible to vote and can request an absentee ballot, if possible.
